OBITUARY REFERENCES
MR. CHAIRMAN: Hon’ble Members, I refer with profound sorrow to the passing 
away of Shri B.K.S. Iyengar, renowned yoga exponent, Shri Lekhraj Bachani, Sardar 
Jagdev Singh Talwandi and Shri S. S. Rajendran, former Members of this House and 
Shri Murli Deora, a sitting Member of this House.
Shri B.K.S. Iyengar passed away on the 20th of August, 2014, at the age of  
96 years. 
Born in December, 1918, in Bellur in Karnataka, Shri Iyengar entered into the 
field of yoga at the age of 16 years. 
Shri Iyengar had been a living legend in the field of yoga and pioneered a style of 
yoga popularly known as ‘Iyengar Yoga’ which is followed by certified yoga teachers 
throughout the world. 
Shri Iyengar is credited with re-discovering the lost art of “Hatha Yoga” and had 
a vast following in more than sixty countries. 
Shri Iyengar had several publications on yoga to his credit, namely, ‘Light on 
Yoga’, ‘Light on Pranayama’, ‘Art of Yoga ’, ‘Yog Dipika’, among others. He was a 
recipient of the Padma Shri in 1991, the Padma Bhushan  in 2002 and the Padma 
Vibhushan in 2014. Shri Iyengar also received international acclaim in the form of a 
Commemorative Stamp issued in his honour by China Post in 2011. His name ‘Iyengar’ 
has also entered the Oxford lexicon as a type of ‘ Astanga Yoga’. 
In the passing away of Shri Iyengar, the country has lost a great personality in 
the field of yoga. His death is an irreparable loss to the world of yoga.

Shri Lekhraj Bachani passed away on the 22nd of August, 2014, at the age of  
85 years. Born in July, 1929, in Sindh, Pakistan, Shri Bachani was educated at the 
M.N. College, Visnagar, Gujarat and Sir L.A. Shah Law College, Ahmedabad. 
A lawyer by profession, Shri Bachani was actively involved in social service. 
He was associated with several educational and religious trusts, cooperative and sports 
movements and social and cultural activities in Gujarat and Rajasthan. 
Shri Bachani started his legislative career as a Member of the Gujarat Legislative 
Assembly in 1972. He was a Member of that Assembly for four consecutive terms, 
i.e., from 1972 to 1975, 1975 to 1980, 1980 to 1985 and 1990 to 1995. He served as 
a Deputy Minister and also as a Minister of State in the Government of Gujarat from 
1975 to 1980 and in 1990. He also served as the Chairman of the Public Accounts 
Committee of the Gujarat Legislative Assembly from 1993 to 1995 and as Chairman 
of the Gujarat State Water Supply and Sewerage Board from 1996 to 1997.
Shri Lekhraj Bachani represented the State of Gujarat in this House from April, 
2000 to April, 2006.
In the passing away of Shri Lekhraj Bachani, the country has lost a distinguished 
parliamentarian and a dedicated social worker.
Sardar Jagdev Singh Talwandi passed away on the 19th of September, 2014,  
at the age of 85 years. 
Sardar Jagdev Singh was born in June, 1929, in Lyalpur District (now in Pakistan). 
An agriculturist, Sardar Jagdev Singh was actively involved in rural upliftment and 
was associated with various social welfare organisations. He was also President of the 
Shiromani Akali Dal. 
Sardar Jagdev Singh started his legislative career as a Member of the Punjab 
Legislative Assembly in 1967 and was a Member of that Assembly from 1967 to 1977. 
He served as a Minister in the Government of Punjab from 1969 to 1971. He was also 
a Member of the Sixth Lok Sabha from 1977 to 1979.
Sardar Jagdev Singh Talwandi represented the State of Punjab in this House from 
July, 1980 to July, 1986. 
In the passing away of Sardar Jagdev Singh Talwandi, the country has lost a 
distinguished parliamentarian and a dedicated social worker. 
Shri S.S. Rajendran passed away on the 24th of October, 2014, at the age of 
86 years. 
Born in December, 1927, Shri Rajendran was educated at the A.M.C.C. School, 
Batlagurdu, Tamil Nadu.

A cine-artist by proression, Shri Rajendran was closely associated with the famous 
drama company, namely, T.K.S. Brothers, from 1940 to 1943 and began his acting 
career in 1952. He acted in about 74 films, produced three films on social issues and 
directed three films. 
A founder member of the South Indian Films Artists’ Association, Shri Rajendran 
served as its Secretary as well as President. He was honoured with awards by the 
State of Tamil Nadu.
Shri S.S. Rajendran started his legislative career as a Member of the Tamil Nadu 
Legislative Assembly in 1962 and was a Member of that Assembly for two terms, from 
1962 to 1970 and again from 1980 to 1984. 
Shri S.S. Rajendran represented the State of Tamil Nadu in this House from 
April, 1970 to April, 1976. 
In the passing away of Shri S. S. Rajendran, the country has lost a noted cine-
artist and an able parliamentarian.
Shri Murli Deora passed away this morning. 
Born in January, 1937, at Bombay in Maharashtra, Shri Murli Deora was a noted 
industrialist. He was also an active social worker. He served as Vice-Chairman of the 
Gandhi Institute of Computer Education and Information Technology of the Bharatiya 
Vidya Bhavan, which provided computer training to the poor and the under-privileged 
youth. As Vice-Chairman of the Indian Red Cross Society, he helped in mobilising 
relief work on many occasions.
Shri Deora served as a Councillor in the Municipal Corporation of Mumbai from 
1968 to 1978 and was the Mayor of Mumbai from 1977 to 1978. 
Shri Deora started his legislative career as a Member of the Maharashtra 
Legislative Council in 1982 and served as a Member of that Council till 1985. He 
was also a Member of the Eighth, Ninth, Tenth and Twelfth Lok Sabha. He served as 
the Chairman of the Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Finance 
from 1998 to 1999. 
Shri  Deora was the International President of the Parliamentarians for Global 
Action, New York from 1995 to 1996 and was the Chairman of the Parliamentarians 
for Global Action, India, from 2002 to 2004. 
Shri Murli Deora represented the State of Maharashtra in this House for three 
terms- from April, 2002 to April, 2008, from April, 2008 to April, 2014 and again 
from April, 2014 till his sad demise. He served in the Union Council of Ministers as 
Minister of Petroleum and Natural Gas from January, 2006 to January, 2011 and as 
Minister of Corporate Affairs from January to July, 2011.

In the passing away of Shri Murli Deora, the country has lost a distinguished 
parliamentarian, an able administrator and a dedicated social worker. 
We deeply mourn the passing away of Shri B. K. S. Iyengar, Shri Lekhraj Bachani, 
Sardar Jagdev Singh Talwandi, Shri S. S. Rajendran and Shri Murli Deora. 
I request Members to rise in their places and observe silence as a mark of respect 
to the memory of the departed. 
(Hon. Members then stood in silence for one minute .)
MR. CHAIRMAN: Secretary-General will convey to the members of the bereaved 
families our sense of profound sorrow and deep sympathy. 
As a mark of respect to the memory of Shri Murli Deora, a sitting Member, the 
House stands adjourned till 11.00 a.m. on Tuesday, the 25th of November, 2014. 
The House then adjourned at fourteen minutes past  
eleven of the clock till eleven of the clock on  
Tuesday, the 25th November, 2014.
